Ability to resolve the most complex, sensitive, or high-impact cybersecurity issues and serve as a senior technical escalation point. Ability to assess significant cybersecurity risks, evaluate complex technical alternatives, and provide authoritative recommendations to management and technical leadership. Ability to establish technical direction and lead development of cybersecurity standards, frameworks, architectures, controls, or long-range technical capabilities. Ability to lead major cybersecurity initiatives involving multiple technical teams, organizational stakeholders, contractors, or external partners. Advanced communication and influencing skills, including the ability to explain complex cybersecurity risks and technical matters to senior technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Ability to provide technical leadership and mentorship without formal supervisory authority. Ability to obtain and maintain relevant advanced industry certifications, as required. As part of our hiring process, we may conduct a skills assessment to better understand an applicant’s proficiency in key areas relevant to the role. Desired Skill and Qualifications We are seeking an experienced, senior-level cybersecurity professional ready to operate at the forefront of US Senate’s cyber defense. The ideal candidate should have: Experience: 7–10 years of progressively responsible cybersecurity experience, including at least 5 years in threat hunting, network forensics, or incident response. Demonstrated success leading complex technical investigations and initiatives in enterprise environments. Network Forensics: Advanced hands-on experience with packet capture, deep packet inspection, traffic reconstruction, and protocol analysis using tools such as Wireshark and Zeek. Strong knowledge of TCP/IP and protocols including HTTP/S, DNS, SMB, FTP, and Kerberos; ability to identify lateral movement, command-and-control activity, and potential data exfiltration. Network Detection: Experience with network monitoring and intrusion detection technologies such as Suricata or Snort, including rule development, tuning, alert analysis, and interpretation of network telemetry. Familiarity with Sigma or YARA is preferred. Threat Hunting: Demonstrated ability to develop, execute, and document hypothesis-driven hunts using threat intelligence, behavioral analytics, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and experience correlating network, endpoint, cloud, and log evidence to reconstruct adversary activity. Detection Engineering: Experience designing, testing, and improving custom detections across SIEM, EDR, and network analytics platforms, including techniques associated with living-off-the-land activity, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and exfiltration. Experience with adversary emulation to validate detection coverage is desirable. Incident Response and Forensics: Ability to lead complex investigations, establish scope and root cause, coordinate containment, and communicate findings. Knowledge of Windows, Linux, and macOS artifacts, operating system internals, and forensic collection and triage methods. Familiarity with Cisco IOS, Solaris, or mobile operating systems is preferred. Technical Leadership: Demonstrated ability to serve as a hands-on technical authority, coordinate cross-functional incident response, mentor colleagues, improve playbooks, and present findings to technical teams, executives, and legislative stakeholders. Automation and Learning: Proficiency in at least one scripting language, such as Python, PowerShell, Bash, Ruby, or Perl, to analyze data and automate investigative workflows. Ability to independently learn emerging technologies and adapt to evolving threats. Work requires occasional walking, standing, bending, and safely carrying items weighing less than 50 pounds, such as laptops, desktops, servers, and routers. Work requires extended periods of computer use. Occasionally, late-night and weekend work is required. Essential Services are functions and activities that are critical to the continuous operation, security, and support of the United States Senate. These services must remain operational without interruption to ensure the Senate can conduct official business. Positions supporting essential services require employees to be available and prepared to work including during inclement weather, holidays, weekends, late nights and overnight hours. Due to the nature of Senate operations, essential services, including network operations and infrastructure, cannot be suspended while the Senate is in session, and maintenance activities may be required outside of normal business hours. Excepted Services refer to functions and activities that are authorized to continue during a lapse of appropriations because they are necessary to the performance of the Senate’s constitutional functions, address emergency circumstances that imminently threaten the safety of human life or the protection of property or directly support essential services of the United States Senate. Employees in excepted positions are generally required to work and remain operational during a lapse of appropriations, to ensure continuity of critical Senate functions. These positions may involve working non-standard schedules, including nights, weekends, holidays, and extended hours, to maintain uninterrupted service and operational readiness. Applicants must be U.S. citizens in order for the SAA to submit your application for a security clearance.

duties: As a Systems and Cloud Engineer, the incumbent serves as a senior technical authority within the Engineering and Operations group, providing expert systems and cloud engineering expertise across the FCC's full technology environment. Designs, engineers, implements, and sustains complex enterprise systems including server environments, virtualization platforms, storage systems, identity and access management platforms, directory services, and cloud-hosted infrastructure in FedRAMP-authorized environments. Ensures that all systems are architected for high availability, fault tolerance, scalability, and security compliance with zero-trust architecture principles consistent with OMB M-22-09. Leads systems modernization and cloud migration engineering initiatives, developing detailed technical designs and implementation plans for migrating FCC on-premises enterprise systems to FedRAMP-authorized cloud platforms. Evaluates existing systems architecture, identifies modernization candidates, and develops migration strategies that minimize operational risk and service disruption while advancing the FCC's cloud-native infrastructure objectives. Designs, engineers, configures, and maintains enterprise systems across Windows Server, Linux distributions, virtualization platforms (e.g., VMware), and enterprise storage systems. Ensures system baselines meet performance, security, and resilience requirements, consistent with E&O engineering patterns. Provides senior engineering support for complex incident resolution, serving as the escalation point for infrastructure and systems incidents that cannot be resolved through routine operations. Diagnoses and resolves complex systems failures, performance degradations, and configuration issues across the FCC's enterprise systems environment. Serves as a senior escalation point for high severity incidents impacting systems, cloud services, identity infrastructure, or hybrid integrations. Performs root cause analysis, permanent corrective actions, and system engineering remediation aligned with the problem management requirements.
